# FAQ-027 Engineering FAQ #27

Revision: Rev A

Q1: What is the required coil cooling water flow for Ring Rolling induction billet heater #1 (EQ-P2-L2-IH01), and why is it critical?
A1: The coil cooling water flow minimum for Ring Rolling induction billet heater #1 (EQ-P2-L2-IH01) is 81 L/min. Background: Adequate coil cooling flow prevents coil overheating, which can cause insulation breakdown, reduced induction efficiency, and accelerated component fatigue. Rationale: The specified minimum maintains heat transfer capacity under expected operating heat loads and provides a margin for transient conditions. Example: If records show the measured flow drops below the specified value during a run, stop heating and investigate pump supply, inlet strainers, and coil connections. Records to keep: log actual measured flow against the specification, note any corrective actions, and attach contemporaneous equipment readings to the job packet. See related procedures in SOP-P2-L1-03 for monitoring methods and ECN-2026-048 for design basis changes.

Q2: What torque is required for the mandrel clamp bolts on Hot Forge radial ring rolling mill #1 (EQ-P2-L1-RR01), and what is the tightening rationale?
A2: The mandrel clamp bolt torque for Hot Forge radial ring rolling mill #1 (EQ-P2-L1-RR01) is 430 N·m. Background: Correct bolt torque ensures consistent clamp preload, minimizing slip and uneven loading during rolling. Rationale: Applying the specified torque achieves the designed clamping force without overstressing threads or bolts, preserving alignment and reducing wear on the mandrel assembly. Example: When replacing a mandrel clamp bolt, use a calibrated torque wrench to apply the stated torque in a controlled sequence, and verify torque on adjacent bolts to ensure uniformity. Records to keep: maintenance entry documenting bolt replacement, tool calibration certificate reference, torque values recorded, and any anomalies. Refer to SOP-P1-L2-02 for torque application procedure and ECN-2026-048 for any bolt material or size updates.

Q3: What is the system pressure limit for Machining hydraulic forging press #2 (EQ-P1-L3-HP02), and how should operators respond if it is approached?
A3: The system pressure limit for Machining hydraulic forging press #2 (EQ-P1-L3-HP02) is 295 bar. Background: The system pressure limit protects hydraulic components and seals from overpressure failure and maintains predictable press behavior. Rationale: Operating within the limit reduces the risk of catastrophic seal failure, hose rupture, and uncontrolled movement. Example: If instrumented pressure approaches the limit during a cycle, suspend the loading activity, isolate the source, and follow lockout and troubleshooting steps. Records to keep: pressure traces for the event, operator notes, corrective action records, and inspection findings. See SOP-P1-L2-02 for hydraulic system isolation and ECN-2026-048 for any updated pressure component qualifications.

Q4: What minimum coil cooling water flow applies to Ring Rolling induction billet heater #2 (EQ-P1-L2-IH02), and how is compliance verified?
A4: The coil cooling water flow minimum for Ring Rolling induction billet heater #2 (EQ-P1-L2-IH02) is 46 L/min. Background: Each induction heater coil has a specific cooling requirement determined by coil geometry and power duty; this minimum prevents localized overheating and maintains coil life. Rationale: Verifying and maintaining the minimum flow reduces thermal cycling stress and preserves electrical insulation. Example: Use the installed flow meter to confirm flow before initiating a heating cycle; if the meter reads below the specified value, do not energize the coil and perform the checklist for water system faults. Records to keep: pre-start checklists showing measured flow, any maintenance actions on the cooling loop, and follow-up verification after repairs. Refer to SOP-P2-L1-03 for flow verification procedure and ECN-2026-048 for history of cooling circuit modifications.

Q5: What is the target billet temperature for Ring Rolling induction billet heater #1 (EQ-P2-L2-IH01), and why must it be controlled?
A5: The target billet temperature for Ring Rolling induction billet heater #1 (EQ-P2-L2-IH01) is 1230 °C. Background: The target billet temperature is selected to obtain required material ductility and metallurgical state prior to ring rolling operations. Rationale: Controlling to the target avoids underheating that can cause cracking and overworking, and avoids overheating that can produce grain growth or undesirable phase changes. Example: Confirm the billet temperature using the calibrated temperature measurement method named in the process SOP before transfer to the rolling mill; if the measured temperature deviates from the target, follow the hold-and-adjust procedure. Records to keep: temperature logs tied to heat IDs, measurement device calibration records, and any corrective actions for temperature deviations. See SOP-P2-L1-03 for measurement technique and SOP-P1-L2-02 for related transfer and handling steps; consult ECN-2026-048 for any changes to target temperature rationale.

Related documents:
- ECN-2026-048
- SOP-P1-L2-02
- SOP-P2-L1-03

Document control note: Maintain records referenced above in the job folder and in the Equipment Maintenance archive per SOP-P1-L2-02.
